ctx1.title: The Missing Lunch Card
ctx1.content: Maya arrived at college early because she had a quiz in the morning. After her first class, she looked in her bag for her lunch card, but it was gone. She checked her jacket pocket, her notebook, and the front desk in the library. Nothing. Maya remembered that she had used the card at the cafeteria the day before. She went back to the cafeteria to ask if anyone had turned it in. A staff member smiled and said, 'Yes, someone left it here after lunch.' Maya felt relieved and thanked the staff member. She decided to keep the card in the same pocket every day after that.

ctx2.title: Roommate Story
ctx2.content: Leah moved into residence on Saturday. Her new roommate, Omar, was quiet at first, but by Sunday evening he was joking with everyone in the hallway. Leah noticed that Omar liked to organize his desk before studying and always listened to music after dinner. On Monday morning, he woke up early, packed his backpack, and left for class with a smile.

c1.title: Community Garden Notice
c1.content: The community garden will be open to members from 8:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m. on weekdays and from 9:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. on weekends. Visitors must sign in at the shed before entering. Tools are available for loan, but they must be returned by the end of the day. Watering is allowed only before 10:00 a.m. on hot days to reduce evaporation.

ctx3.title: Energy-Saving Upgrade
ctx3.content: A homeowner spends about $2,400 each year on electricity. After replacing old light bulbs with LED bulbs, the bill may drop by about $180 per year. If the home later adds a window air conditioner, the annual bill could increase by about $250.

ctx4.title: Kitchen Safety Tips
ctx4.content: To keep food safe, the refrigerator should stay at or below 4°C. Raw meat should be stored on the bottom shelf so juices do not drip onto other foods. Surfaces should be cleaned with hot, soapy water after preparing meals. Leftovers should be cooled and placed in the refrigerator within two hours.

ctx5.title: Community Garden News
ctx5.content: The community garden uses rain barrels to collect water for plants. Volunteers also spread mulch around the vegetables to keep the soil moist. During summer, the garden depends on compost, which helps return nutrients to the soil and reduces waste.
